chapter: Berlin and the Turner and Bryant bands
title: Band teasing: Long John Silver, Gorilla and 'Master Race'
summary: He describes how big-band musicians needle each other with nicknames and cowbells, and how thin-skinned players quit because of it.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Cut out where the trombone player says "Master race."
Was that a nickname they had for him, was it a joke?
These people, in all big bands, they going to get on you. They called me one time, they called me John Silver.

So I told Jimmy now, I was laughing with them because he couldn't get me. They had a big old boy up there, very big, tall boy. They used to call him Gorilla. But see, when you messed with gorilla, you had to leave because Gorilla always
could fix you up. And they said, "Oh, Gorilla," he said, "All right, Master Race."

"Fellows; I don't like that old, rough kidding." We say, "Well, Master Race, you call him Gorilla, everybody call him that." "Yeah, but I -- (unintelligible). Then everybody says, "Look, I told you, don't call him that." The bass player would tell the piano player, "please don't call him that now." "What do you mean, don't call him what?" You know, So then he said, all right, fellows, (unintelligible). And see, they'd get on him man, and if you are thin skinned, man, you're in trouble.

Some people, sometimes, I would quit the band on account of that. Oh, yes. For example, you get in there and you miss a note, cat would have a bell up there, ding, ding. (Laughter.) The trumpets you might miss the notes, you know. And that Matthews, he would get on that trombone and he got up there and he brought a big cow bell. "Fellows, let's stop that kind of stuff."
